panel_intro: One question at a time — nothing here is submitted anywhere.

location.text: Is the vehicle stopped somewhere unsafe — a travel lane or similar?

symptom.text: When you turn the key or press start, what happens?

options.label: Nothing at all — no sound, no lights
A clicking sound, but it doesn't start
Lights and radio work, but it won't start

jump_available.text: Do you have jumper cables or a jump box, and another vehicle or way to jump it?

recurring.text: Has this happened before recently, even after a jump or charge?

options.label: No, this is the first time

unsafe_location.title: Move Only to Immediate Safety
unsafe_location.summary: A dead battery isn't urgent by itself, but an unsafe location is. If you can safely move a short distance, do that first.
unsafe_location.confidence_text: Location safety always outranks the battery question itself.
not_to_do: Don't attempt a jump start while in or near a travel lane.
Don't stand behind the vehicle in traffic to work on it.
Don't wait where you are hoping it resolves itself.
before_help_checklist: Turn on hazard lights before and after moving.
Check mirrors and traffic before moving at all.
Once safely stopped, exit on the side away from traffic.
Call roadside assistance once you're safely off the road.

phone_script.intro: Read this once you're safely stopped and calling for help.
lines: Hi, my battery seems dead and I'm now safely stopped at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA for a jump start?

unsafe_location.next_action: Once you're safely off the road, use this tool again if anything about the situation has changed.

possible_starter.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
possible_starter.summary: Lights and radio working but no start usually points away from a simple dead battery — a starter or ignition issue is more likely. A technician can confirm on the spot.
possible_starter.confidence_text: This pattern is a common starter/ignition signal, but only a technician with the right tools can confirm it.
not_to_do: Don't keep cranking the key repeatedly — that can drain the battery further and heat up the starter.
Don't assume a jump will fix it if the battery isn't actually the issue.
Don't ignore a repeat of this pattern — get it diagnosed properly.
before_help_checklist: Note any clicking, grinding, or silence when you try to start it.
Turn off accessories while you wait.
Have your keys and vehicle location ready.
Stay with the vehicle if it's safe to do so.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, my lights and radio work but the car won't start. I'm at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA and whether this sounds like a starter issue to you?

possible_starter.next_action: Ask the shop to test the starter and ignition switch, not just the battery.

roadside_battery.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
roadside_battery.summary: No way to jump it yourself means a roadside jump-start call is the practical next step.
roadside_battery.confidence_text: This is a textbook roadside-assistance case.
not_to_do: Don't keep cranking the key — it heats up the starter and drains what's left of the battery.
Don't accept a ride from a stranger instead of a real roadside service.
Don't assume it's definitely the battery until it's tested.
before_help_checklist: Turn off accessories (lights, AC, radio) while you wait.
Have your keys and vehicle location ready.
Note if this has happened before.
Stay with the vehicle if it's safe to do so.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, my vehicle won't start — I think it's the battery. I'm at [location description].
It's safe to approach and I'm waiting nearby.
Can you confirm ETA and whether a jump start is included?

roadside_battery.next_action: If it dies again soon after, get the battery and alternator tested rather than just jumping it again.

possible_alternator.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
possible_alternator.summary: A battery that keeps dying even after being jumped or charged usually means the alternator isn't recharging it while you drive. Driving off on a fresh jump can leave you stranded again, potentially somewhere worse.
possible_alternator.confidence_text: This pattern strongly suggests an alternator or charging-system issue, but only a shop can confirm it with a load test.
not_to_do: Don't assume another jump start solves the underlying problem.
Don't drive further than necessary on a battery that keeps dying.
Don't ignore dimming lights or electrical issues while driving — that's often an early warning.
before_help_checklist: Note how many times this has happened and over what timeframe.
Mention any dimming headlights or electrical flickering.
Confirm exactly where you want the vehicle taken.
Keep your keys and paperwork accessible for the driver.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my battery keeps dying even after a jump. I'm at [location description].
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?
I suspect it's the alternator, not just the battery.

possible_alternator.next_action: Ask the shop to test the alternator's charging output, not just replace the battery.

jump_start.title: Safe to Reassess — Try a Jump Start
jump_start.summary: A one-time dead battery with cables and a donor vehicle on hand is a reasonable case to try jumping it yourself.
jump_start.confidence_text: This assumes a standard 12V system and no other visible damage. If it doesn't start after a proper attempt, stop and call for help instead.
not_to_do: Don't connect the negative cable directly to the dead battery's negative terminal — use a metal ground point instead.
Don't let the cable clamps touch each other while connected.
Don't crank the starter for more than about 10 seconds at a time.
before_help_checklist: Connect positive to positive first, then negative to a metal ground on the dead vehicle.
Let the donor vehicle run for a couple of minutes before attempting to start.
Start the dead vehicle, then remove cables in reverse order.
Let it run for a while afterward to recharge before shutting it off again.

phone_script.intro: Keep this ready in case the jump doesn't work.
lines: Hi, my battery died and a jump start didn't work. I'm at [location description].
Can you confirm ETA for roadside assistance?

jump_start.next_action: If it starts, get the battery tested soon — a jump gets you moving, it doesn't diagnose the cause.
